app.title: GC×GC Chemical Insight Workbench
app.summary: The person picks a calibration route. They either choose one of the published reference instrument programs, or enter their own method details and upload n-alkane and calibration-standard tables so the instrument parameters can be fitted. Next they supply analyte retention times, from a built-in named set or an uploaded table, and can add a detector-intensity chromatogram. One button then computes every property model for every analyte. In the explorer they choose a domain and a property, read its contour map with the analytes plotted on it, look at the values and model evidence, and compare properties. They can also check the chromatogram, biological-system views and calibration diagnostics, then download wide or long result tables and a metadata file.

task.text: Turn two-dimensional retention times of chemicals into screening estimates of many physicochemical, environmental and biological properties, with calibration and applicability checks.

data.text: Tables of retention times in two chromatographic dimensions for named analytes. A custom calibration adds n-alkane retention tables and calibration-standard tables with solvation descriptors. An optional chromatogram table gives detector intensity over the two retention axes.
data.item: a named analyte with a first- and second-dimension retention time

stage.text: estimating properties from calibrated retention data after peaks are identified, before screening decisions

mechanism.text: A stepwise form gathers the calibration route, the input tables and an optional intensity map, then computes all the models at once. A workspace switcher opens a property explorer: a category and a searchable property picker drive a contour map with the analytes overlaid, a guide card, and tabs for values, comparison and model evidence. Other workspaces show the chromatogram with an analyte search, biological-system modules, calibration diagnostics and downloads.

field.text: retention-based property estimation (linear free energy relationships) with comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography in environmental chemistry

workflow.name: calibrate a measurement and predict properties of each item from published models

steps.step: choose or fit the calibration that maps measurements onto the model's scale
steps.here: A radio picks a published reference program (A, B or C) or the advanced route. The advanced route needs a stationary-phase confirmation box, method metadata, and n-alkane and calibration-chemical uploads, and fits alpha1, alpha2 and alpha3.
Use the named paper analytes or upload a name/t1/t2 table. A full chromatogram intensity table is optional. Templates and formatting examples can be downloaded.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: 'Calculate 51 properties' (or 'Fit alpha parameters and calculate 51 properties') runs every model on every analyte and shows the fitted parameters as metrics.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Pills pick a scientific domain, and a search box narrows the property list before one property is selected.

The selected property gets a guide card (unit, family, cautions), a contour map over the two coordinates with the analytes overlaid, and tabs for its calculated values, paper examples and model evidence (n, R², RMSE, equation, source).
A multiselect puts up to four properties from the category side by side as columns for every analyte.
The Tables & quality workspace shows calibration diagnostics against the published programs and coverage counts, then offers downloads: a wide CSV, a long CSV and a JSON metadata file.

distinctive: A calibration-transfer route fits instrument parameters from user standards and compares the fit statistics with the published reference programs
Each property is drawn as a contour field over the two-dimensional retention coordinates, so analytes can be read off a map
Every model carries its source reference, equation, training size and applicability cautions, and extrapolation outside the calibration range is counted
The chromatogram shows the analytes as a peak map, or as a continuous intensity map when an intensity table is supplied

parts.title: New analysis
parts.summary: A stepwise form for choosing the calibration route, uploading the alkane, calibration, analyte and intensity tables, and running every property model.

parts.title: Property explorer
parts.summary: Choose a domain and search for a property, then read its guide, map, analyte values, paper examples, comparison table and model evidence.

parts.title: GC×GC property map
parts.summary: A contour field of the selected property over the two retention coordinates, with the analytes plotted on top and hover values.

parts.title: GC×GC chromatogram
parts.summary: Shows the analyte peaks, or a detector-intensity map, on the two retention axes, with a name search over the analyte table.

parts.title: Quality & applicability
parts.summary: Shows calibration diagnostics, fitted parameters, fit statistics against the published programs, coverage counts, environmental-behaviour regions and model warnings.
